name: TREND
description: TREND returns values along a linear trend line fitted by least squares to known data, predicting one or many y-values for the supplied x-values. It is an array function.
tldr: Fits a linear trend and returns predicted y-values (array).

parameters.name: known_ys
parameters.description: The dependent (y) values of the known data used to fit the line.

parameters.name: known_xs
parameters.description: The independent (x) values of the known data; defaults to 1,2,3,... if omitted.

parameters.name: new_xs
parameters.description: The x-values at which to predict y. If omitted, the known x-values are reused.

parameters.name: const
parameters.description: TRUE (or omitted) includes an intercept; FALSE forces the line through the origin.

basicExample.explanation: The fitted line is y = -1 + 2.2x, so at x=6 the prediction is 12.2 (same as FORECAST).

advancedExamples.title: Predict several points at once
advancedExamples.description: Supply an array of new x-values to get an array of predictions
advancedExamples.explanation: Spills two values: 12.2 at x=6 and 14.4 at x=7. In older Excel, confirm with Ctrl+Shift+Enter; in Microsoft 365 it spills automatically.

advancedExamples.title: Force line through origin
advancedExamples.explanation: The fitted line passes through (0,0); useful when theory requires a zero intercept.

howItWorks: TREND performs ordinary least-squares linear regression (y = a + bx) on the known data, then evaluates that line at each value in new_xs. Because it accepts an array for new_xs, it can return many predictions in one formula. Text, logicals, and blanks in the known arrays are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Provide known data
howToSteps.text: List known y-values and, optionally, known x-values.

howToSteps.name: Provide new x-values
howToSteps.text: List the x-points you want to predict (a single cell or a range).

howToSteps.name: Enter as array
howToSteps.text: Type =TREND(known_ys, known_xs, new_xs) and press Enter (or Ctrl+Shift+Enter in legacy Excel).

limitations: Models only a linear relationship; use GROWTH for exponential patterns.
known_xs and known_ys must have the same number of points, or #REF! is returned.
Returns an array, so in pre-dynamic Excel it must be entered as an array formula and needs enough empty cells to spill into.

commonErrors.cause: known_xs and known_ys differ in size, or new_xs cannot spill into the needed cells.
commonErrors.fix: Match the known array sizes and ensure output cells are empty.

commonErrors.cause: A non-numeric or mis-shaped argument was supplied.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: TREND works as an array function in Google Sheets, returning a row/column of predictions.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Identical behavior; results spill across cells in Sheets too.

faq.question: How is TREND different from FORECAST?
faq.answer: FORECAST returns a single predicted y; TREND can return an entire array of predictions at once.

faq.question: Does TREND need array entry?
faq.answer: In Microsoft 365 it spills automatically; in older Excel use Ctrl+Shift+Enter.

faq.question: Can TREND fit through the origin?
faq.answer: Yes, set the const argument to FALSE to force the line through (0,0).
